title: CISA Cybersecurity Advisory AA24-131A: Threat Actor Exploits Known Vulnerabilities in Network Appliances
content:
CISA, in collaboration with the FBI and international partners, has identified ongoing exploitation of known vulnerabilities in network edge devices. Threat actors are targeting organizations that have not applied available patches to their VPN concentrators and firewall appliances.

AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- FortiGate SSL-VPN (CVE-2023-27997) — heap buffer overflow allowing remote code execution
- Cisco ASA and FTD (CVE-2024-20359) — persistent local code execution via crafted firmware image
- Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2024-21887) — command injection in web interface

IMPACT:
Successful exploitation allows threat actors to establish persistent access, exfiltrate credentials, move laterally within networks, and deploy ransomware. Multiple critical infrastructure sectors have been affected, including healthcare, energy, and financial services.

MITIGATION STEPS:
1. Apply vendor-supplied patches immediately for all listed CVEs.
2. Reset all credentials that may have traversed compromised appliances.
3. Enable multi-factor authentication on all remote access points.
4. Monitor network traffic for indicators of compromise listed in Appendix A.
5. Segment network access to limit lateral movement from edge devices.
6. Review and restrict administrative access to management interfaces.

SEVERITY: Critical
CVSS SCORES: CVE-2023-27997 (9.8), CVE-2024-20359 (6.0), CVE-2024-21887 (8.2)

Organizations that believe they have been compromised should contact CISA at report@cisa.gov or call (888) 282-0870.
